![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14098036/assets/981252abc3668e62a5c9289c918d1231ec9a83745f70a00f0da4c85f194b8215.png)

The graph above shows the velocity of an object moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis. At time $t=4,$ the particle is located at the position $x=-3.$ What is the position of the particle at time $t=7?$

The position of the particle at $t=7$ is $x=$
{{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
The position of the particle at $t=7$ is equal to its position at $t=4$ plus the total displacement over $t\in [4,7].$ Therefore, we can calculate it as follows:

$$
x(7)=x(4)+{\int }_{4}^{7}v(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

We are told that $x(4)=-3$, and we can compute the integral ${\int }_{4}^{7}v(t)\,\text{d}t$ by finding the signed area under the graph from $t=4$ to $t=7.$ Computing the signed area, we get

$$
{\int }_{4}^{7}v(t)\,\text{d}t=3.
$$

Therefore,

$$
x(7)=-3+3=0.
$$

So the position of the particle at $t=7$ is $x=0.$
